subject: music
topicDisplay: Unit A2 3 Responding To Music Set Works And Comparative Study
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: A pivot chord in modulation is best defined as which of the following?
options: A chord borrowed from the parallel major
A chord common to both the old and new keys used to effect the change
The final chord of a phrase only
A chromatic chord with no diatonic function
questions.explain: A pivot chord belongs diatonically to both keys, smoothing the transition during a modulation.

questions.q: In music production, 'panning' controls...?
options: The amount of reverb on a track
The placement of a sound within the stereo field (left to right)
The overall loudness of the master
questions.explain: Panning positions a sound across the stereo image from left to right.

questions.q: A 'riff' in rock and pop music is best defined as...?
options: A short, repeated melodic or rhythmic pattern, often instrumental
questions.explain: A riff is a short, catchy pattern repeated throughout a song, frequently as an instrumental hook.

questions.q: Which composer is often called the 'father of the symphony' and the 'father of the string quartet'?
questions.explain: Haydn's extensive output shaped both the Classical symphony and the string quartet.

questions.q: An interrupted cadence most commonly progresses from which chord to which?
questions.explain: An interrupted (deceptive) cadence moves from V to vi, thwarting the expected resolution to the tonic.

questions.q: A German augmented sixth chord contains which intervals above the bass?
options: Major third, augmented fourth and augmented sixth
Major third and augmented sixth only
Major third, perfect fifth and augmented sixth
questions.explain: The German sixth comprises a major third, perfect fifth and augmented sixth above the bass note.

questions.q: Which composer wrote the Brandenburg Concertos?
questions.explain: J. S. Bach composed the six Brandenburg Concertos, exemplars of the late Baroque concerto.

questions.q: Vivaldi's 'The Four Seasons' is an example of which Baroque genre?
questions.explain: 'The Four Seasons' consists of four solo violin concertos, a leading Baroque solo-concerto example.

questions.q: A circle-of-fifths progression characteristically moves the bass by which interval?
questions.explain: A circle-of-fifths sequence moves root by root down a fifth (equivalently up a fourth) each step.

questions.q: In a Classical concerto first movement, the cadenza traditionally occurs at which point?
options: Near the end, over a tonic six-four before the final tutti
At the very opening before the orchestra plays
In the middle of the development only
questions.explain: The cadenza, a virtuosic solo passage, typically falls near the movement's end on a cadential six-four leading to the closing tutti.

questions.q: The standard twelve-bar blues progression in its basic form follows which sequence of chords (in bars)?
questions.explain: The classic twelve-bar blues uses four bars of I, two of IV returning to I, then V-IV-I across the final four bars.

questions.q: A Picardy third refers to which feature?
options: A chord built on the third degree
A minor-key piece ending on a major (raised third) tonic chord
A third added above the melody
A major piece ending on the minor third
questions.explain: A tierce de Picardie raises the third of the final tonic chord so a minor-key work ends on a major chord.

questions.q: Sonata form consists of which three main sections?
questions.explain: Sonata form unfolds in exposition, development and recapitulation, often with an introduction and coda.

questions.q: In the genre of the stage musical, an 'I want' song typically functions to...?
options: Resolve the plot in the finale
Express a principal character's central desire or goal early in the show
questions.explain: The 'I want' song establishes the protagonist's driving desire, usually near the start of a musical.

questions.q: In film music, 'underscoring' (or underscore) most accurately means...?
options: Background music supporting a scene's mood or action, typically not heard by the characters
A loud climactic fanfare during the titles
The lyrics printed beneath a song
Music that the on-screen characters can hear (diegetic music)
questions.explain: Underscoring is non-diegetic background music that supports a scene's emotional or dramatic content.

questions.q: Which mode results from playing the white notes from D to D?
questions.explain: The Dorian mode runs from D to D on the white notes, with a minor third but a major sixth.

questions.q: A retardation differs from a suspension in which way?
options: It resolves upward by step rather than downward
questions.explain: A retardation is a suspended note that resolves upward by step, whereas a suspension resolves downward.

questions.q: 'Sequencing' in music production primarily involves...?
options: Mastering a finished album for vinyl
Arranging musical events (often MIDI) in time on a DAW timeline for playback or editing
Adding distortion to a guitar amplifier
questions.explain: Sequencing arranges and edits musical events, frequently MIDI data, along a timeline for playback.

questions.q: 'Scat singing' in jazz is...?
options: Singing only the written lyrics with no variation
Singing in strict unison with the bass line
Vocal improvisation using nonsense syllables to imitate an instrument
questions.explain: Scat singing improvises wordless, nonsense syllables, treating the voice like an improvising instrument.

questions.q: Serialism, as developed by Schoenberg, organises pitches using which device?
questions.explain: Schoenberg's twelve-tone (serial) method orders all twelve chromatic pitches into a tone row that governs the music.

questions.q: A perfect cadence is formed by which progression?
questions.explain: A perfect (authentic) cadence moves from the dominant (V) to the tonic (I).

questions.q: A fugue opens with which compositional procedure?
options: A subject stated alone then imitated by successive voices
questions.explain: A fugue begins with a subject announced in one voice, answered imitatively by entering voices.

questions.q: Which jazz style, emerging in the 1940s, is defined by fast tempos, complex chord substitutions and virtuosic improvisation, associated with Charlie Parker and Dizzy Gillespie?
questions.explain: Bebop is the fast, harmonically complex and virtuosic jazz style pioneered by Parker and Gillespie.

questions.q: Which key signature has four sharps?
questions.explain: E major has four sharps: F sharp, C sharp, G sharp and D sharp.

questions.q: In figured bass, the symbol '6' beneath a bass note indicates which chord position?
questions.explain: A bare '6' indicates a first-inversion triad, with the bass note a sixth and a third above it.

questions.q: The whole-tone scale, favoured by Debussy, divides the octave into how many equal steps?
questions.explain: The whole-tone scale consists of six pitches a whole tone apart, lacking semitones and a clear tonic.

questions.q: Swing-era big bands such as Count Basie's typically organised their players into which sectional layout?
questions.explain: Big bands are built around a saxophone section, a brass section and a rhythm section.

questions.q: A tonic pedal is best described as which device?
options: A sustained tonic note held while harmonies change above it
A rapid alternation of tonic and dominant
A melodic ornament on the tonic
A modulation to the tonic minor
questions.explain: A pedal is a sustained or repeated note, the tonic pedal holding the tonic while other parts move through changing harmonies.

questions.q: Which woodwind instrument was a notable addition to the orchestra during the Classical-to-Romantic expansion?
questions.explain: The clarinet became a standard orchestral instrument from the late Classical period onward.

questions.q: A homophonic texture is characterised by which?
options: A melody supported by chordal accompaniment
Two or more independent equal melodic lines
questions.explain: Homophony features a principal melody accompanied by chords, all parts moving largely together.
